subject: Archaeology
title: Ötzi the Iceman
description: Learn Ötzi the Iceman in one minute.

hook.text: In 1991, hikers in the Alps found a body sticking out of melting ice. They thought it was a recent accident.

buildup.text: The body turned out to be 5,300 years old — a man from the Copper Age, preserved with all his gear.

discovery.text: Ötzi carried a copper axe, a bow, arrows, and medicinal herbs. His shoes had insulated grass padding.

twist.text: A CT scan revealed an arrowhead in his shoulder. Ötzi was murdered — shot from behind while fleeing.

climax.text: DNA analysis found his descendants alive in Austria today. His last meal was deer and unleavened bread.

punchline.text: A 5,300-year-old murder case was solved by a hospital CT scanner.

quiz.question: How did scientists determine that Ötzi was murdered?
options: They found a knife wound on his skeleton
A CT scan revealed an arrowhead lodged in his shoulder
Written records from his era described the killing

details.summary: Ötzi the Iceman, found in the Italian Alps in 1991, is a naturally mummified man who died around 3300 BCE. His body, clothing, tools, and stomach contents survived frozen for 5,300 years, providing an unparalleled portrait of Copper Age life in prehistoric Europe.
details.whyItMatters: Ötzi is the best-preserved prehistoric human ever found. His complete toolkit, clothing, tattoos, last meals, and cause of death provide more information about a single individual from prehistory than any other source.
takeaways: A 5,300-year-old mummified body found in the Italian Alps in 1991
Preserved with complete clothing, tools, and stomach contents
He was murdered — an arrowhead was found lodged in his shoulder

faq.question: How did Ötzi die exactly?
faq.answer: A flint arrowhead lodged in his left shoulder severed an artery, causing fatal blood loss. He also had a deep cut on his right hand from a fight shortly before death. CT scans revealed head trauma suggesting he may have been struck after being shot. This was a murder, not an accident.

faq.question: What did Ötzi's belongings reveal about Copper Age life?
faq.answer: He carried a copper axe, flint knife, bow and arrows, birch-bark containers, and medicinal fungi. His clothing included a bear-fur hat, goat-skin leggings, and a grass cloak. His last meals included ibex meat and einkorn wheat, indicating a mixed hunting-farming lifestyle.
